prompt.text:
Build an interactive 3D web experience of an Alpine Waterwheel Sawmill & Blacksmith Trip-Hammer Forge set in a sunlit mountain gorge.

The scene and experience should include:

1. Setting & structures: A weathered stone-and-timber watermill with an adjoining open-bay blacksmith forge beside a rocky mountain stream and flume, framed by gorge rock faces, a small stone footbridge, pine trees, stacked timber logs, mossy boulders, a coal hearth, quench barrel, and workbench tools.

2. Coupled water-to-machine mechanics:
- An interactive sluice gate control (0% to 100% flow) that regulates water pouring down the wooden flume onto an overshot waterwheel.
- Water flow physically drives the wheel speed, which in turn drives the interior shaft and gear train powering:
- A reciprocating frame-saw cutting a timber log on a moving carriage.
- Pumping forge bellows that brighten the hearth coals as airflow increases.
- A cam-driven trip-hammer striking a glowing hot iron billet on the anvil with impact sparks when the hammer drops.
- Closing the sluice gate smoothly coasts the wheel, gears, saw, bellows, and hammer to a stop.

3. Inspection & controls:
- A cutaway / open-mill toggle that opens the roof and wall shutters so the entire interior gear train, linkages, saw, bellows, and trip-hammer can be inspected clearly in motion, with nothing hidden inside empty shells.
- Smooth orbit/zoom camera controls plus quick camera presets (wide gorge establishing view, sluice & waterwheel, sawmill mechanism interior, and forge trip-hammer & anvil close-up).

Important guidance

Original imaginary scene: This is a fictional world, not a real-world landmark. Strict 1:1 matching of incidental 2D concept details or ornament counts is not required. Do not waste time nitpicking minor sketch variations. Prioritize convincing 3D craft, crisp close-up materials and lighting, clean focus, and rock-solid working mechanics.

Plan first, wait for go-ahead: Do not start building yet. do your upfront inspection and planning, present the complete plan, and wait for my explicit go-ahead. Once approved, I will let you run unattended.

prompt.text:
Create one animated SVG illustration and save it to:
<output folder>\<model>.svg

The subject
A pelican riding a zebra, and the zebra is itself riding a horse. That is a three-animal stack: the horse runs along the ground carrying the zebra on its back, and the zebra carries the pelican on its back. All three must be clearly recognisable as what they are.

Make it as detailed as possible
- This is judged on richness and craft. Flat, simple, icon-like drawings will look weak. Go far beyond basic shapes.
- Draw real anatomy: the pelican's long bill and throat pouch, plumage, wings and webbed feet; the zebra's stripe pattern over its whole body, mane, ears and muzzle; the horse's musculature, jointed legs, hooves, mane and tail.
- Use shading, gradients, highlights and shadows so the animals have form and depth. Add tack or props if you like (saddle, reins, goggles), and a full background environment with depth.
- It will be shown at up to 1080 px, so fine detail is visible and rewarded.

Animation
- The horse moves in a believable gait with all four legs jointed and cycling, travelling through the scene (the scenery scrolls past).
- The riders react to the motion: bodies bob in time, the zebra holds on, the pelican balances. Add secondary motion wherever it helps, such as mane, tail, feathers, pouch, ears, dust, clouds.
- More motion, and more convincing motion, is better.

Technical requirements
- A single self-contained .svg file: no JavaScript, no external images, fonts, stylesheets or links. Animate with SMIL and/or CSS only.
- The root element uses viewBox="0 0 1000 1000" (square) and has a full opaque background.
- The animation starts by itself when the file is opened in a browser and loops forever. The whole scene repeats exactly every 6 seconds: every animation's duration must divide evenly into 6 s (for example 0.5 s, 0.6 s, 1 s, 1.5 s, 2 s, 3 s or 6 s), so the frame at 6.0 s matches the frame at 0.0 s.
- It must render correctly in current Chrome.
- No text of any kind in the image, and nothing that identifies you, any AI model or any company.

How to work
- This is a one-shot test: design and write the complete file once, yourself. Do not render, screenshot or preview it, do not search the web, do not use subagents, and do not revise the design after you have written it.
- There is no size limit, but a finished file beats an unfinished ambitious one: make sure the file is complete, valid XML and saved. If saving fails for a technical reason you may save again, in several parts if needed, without changing the design.
- Do not create any other files.
- When the file is saved, reply with one line: the file path, then a one-sentence description of what you drew.

prompt.text: Build an unbroken 20-second one-shot cinematic Three.js architectural and nature benchmark of a rain-washed Kyoto Senbon Torii shrine path winding into a sunlit Arashiyama bamboo grove at golden dawn. SCENE & ATMOSPHERIC FIDELITY: Sculpt authentic rows of weathered vermilion-red Torii gates with curved black kasagi roof caps, granite kamebara plinths, and subtle lacquer specular sheen; wet dark flagstone steps glistening with realistic puddle reflections; moss-covered granite stone lanterns (toro) glowing softly with warm inner candle light; a clear shallow mountain stream with gentle ripples under a mossy stone footbridge; slowly drifting crimson maple leaves (momiji); and a dense towering emerald bamboo grove with segmented culms and layered leafy canopy (never blocky low-poly flat paper trees). LIGHTING & VOLUMETRIC GOD-RAYS: Cast rich golden early-morning sunlight diagonally through the bamboo canopy and between the vermilion Torii pillars to create soft volumetric Tyndall god-rays piercing delicate drifting morning mist, balancing deep mossy shadows against luminous wet stone highlights. ONE-SHOT STEADICAM CHOREOGRAPHY: (1) t=0s to 8s — Glide smoothly at ~1.4m eye level forward through the curving vermilion Senbon Torii corridor over wet reflective stone steps as diagonal golden sunbeams and drifting maple leaves pass through the frame. (2) t=8s to 14s — Emerge onto a mossy stone shrine terrace beside glowing stone lanterns and the shallow stream reflecting red Torii gates and floating maple leaves. (3) t=14s to 20s — Gently glide forward and tilt smoothly upward to frame the towering sunlit bamboo grove, golden mist god-rays, and a distant hillside wooden shrine roof silhouette glowing in dawn light. No text or UI.

prompt.text:
TASK
Create a 3D model in Blender: an ancient Norse war-king's throne from a
dark-fantasy world. It should feel heavy, old, grim and powerful.

What I want to see:
- Size: about 2.2 m tall without the antlers, about 2.8 m tall with them.
Wide and massive.
- Base: a stepped platform of dark, weathered stone with carved
interlaced Norse knotwork on the front step.
- Backrest: tall, arched, made of vertical dark wooden planks. Two
intertwined serpent-dragons are carved in relief on it, their bodies
braided together, heads facing each other at the top.
- Top: a deer skull with huge antlers, mounted inside an iron ring at
the top of the backrest and bound with rope.
- Side posts: two thick carved wooden posts covered in knotwork,
reinforced with riveted iron bands. A large bearded battle axe is
mounted on top of each post, blades facing outward.
- Banners: a tattered dark-red cloth banner hangs from an iron rod on each
side, below the axes, with a pale Norse symbol on it. The bottom edges
are torn and frayed.
- Armrests: ending in carved snarling wolf or dragon heads with open jaws.
- Seat: draped with a heavy, torn dark-red cloth with a woven knotwork
stripe down the middle, hanging over the front edge.
- Wear: old cracked wood, dull dark iron and bronze, dirt and dust in the
carvings, faded and frayed fabric. Very textured and highly detailed.
It must look ancient and real, not clean, not plastic, not cartoony.

The exact shapes, carving patterns and smaller details are up to you.

WORKING FOLDER
Your working folder is: [FOLDER]
Save all files there and nowhere else.

SETUP
- You must work through the Blender MCP connection only.
- Before doing anything else, check the Blender MCP connection. If you cannot
connect, STOP immediately and tell me. Do not try to work around it (no
writing scripts for me to run manually, no other tools).
- Start from an empty scene: delete all default objects first.
- You can and should look at the viewport and renders through the MCP to check
and improve your work.
- There is no limit on iterations. Keep working until you consider the result
finished. Work autonomously and do not ask me questions.

RULES
- Create everything yourself inside Blender: modeling, sculpting, modifiers,
geometry nodes, shader nodes, procedural textures, cloth simulation,
texture painting and baking are all allowed.
- Stay inside your working folder. Do NOT read, list, search or open any
files or folders outside it (no browsing my other projects, user folders,
config files, or other drives). The only things you may access are your
working folder and Blender through the MCP.
- Inside Blender, do not open, append or link any other .blend files.
- You MAY use the internet only for Blender / Python API documentation and
technical help.
- You MUST NOT download or import any ready-made models, textures, images,
HDRIs, materials, add-ons, asset packs or asset libraries (including the Poly
Haven, Sketchfab and Hyper3D/Rodin integrations, if your MCP offers them).
- You MUST NOT search for or look at reference images of thrones or similar
objects.
- You MUST NOT use external AI generators (image, texture or 3D).
- Do not read or write any memory, notes or rules files, and do not use
knowledge from my previous projects. Work only from this prompt.

POLYGON BUDGET
- The throne must be between 150,000 and 200,000 triangles, counted with
all modifiers evaluated, as shown in Blender's scene statistics.
- Fine detail beyond that budget must come from materials (procedural
textures, bump/normal maps, or baked maps you generated yourself).
- Scene elements other than the throne (a ground plane, a backdrop) must
stay simple: max 2,000 triangles in total.

PRESENTATION
- I will record a video myself by orbiting around the throne in the Blender
viewport (Rendered shading mode), so it must look impressive in real time
from every angle.
- Use EEVEE as the render engine. All materials and effects must look good in
EEVEE viewport rendering.
- Place the throne at the world origin, standing on the ground, with its
object origin at the center of the throne so it orbits nicely.
- Set up lighting, world background and atmosphere for a dark-fantasy mood
that works from ALL viewing angles, not just from one camera. Use only
Blender lights, world shaders and volumetrics, no external HDRIs.
- The scene must stay smooth in the viewport: no effects that make real-time
orbiting laggy.
- Save to the working folder:
- throne.blend
- render_hero.png: one EEVEE still at 1080x1920 as a thumbnail.

FINAL REPORT
When you are done, report:
- the final triangle count of the throne
- a short description of how you made it (techniques, materials, carvings)
- confirmation that no external assets were used

prompt.text:
# Task: a mind-blowing, photoreal 3D luxury mechanical chronograph that explodes into every one of its parts and reassembles, in one HTML file, plus a cinematic MP4

This is a public showcase that will be posted on X, side by side with another AI model given this exact prompt. People will judge it in the first two seconds, so it must look like a real watch photographed by a high-end watch photographer with a macro lens, not a toy built from cylinders. Make it as ultra-realistic and as insanely detailed as you possibly can: real micro-mechanics, real finishing, real light on real metal. Do not disappoint.

## Your folder
Work ONLY inside: `{{FOLDER}}` (create it if missing). Don't read, write or delete anything outside it, apart from tool installs and caches. If you need a local HTTP server, use a random high port (e.g. 4xxxx), never 3000/5173/8000/8080.

## Deliverables (all in your folder)
1. `chronograph.html`: ONE self-contained HTML file.
- The only external dependency allowed is Three.js (core plus `examples/jsm` addons) loaded from an exact pinned version on jsdelivr or unpkg via an import map. Nothing else external: no downloaded 3D models (GLB/OBJ/FBX), no image textures, no HDRI files, no font files. Text on the dial may be drawn with canvas 2D using fonts already installed in the browser/OS, or built as geometry. Every mesh, material, procedural texture (sunray and guilloché dial finishes, perlage, Côtes de Genève stripes, brushing, engraving, leather grain, printed dial scales) and the environment lighting must be generated in code inside that file.
- Opened in a browser it is an interactive watch studio:
- orbit and zoom, all the way down to extreme macro (a few millimetres from the parts);
- an Explode slider from fully assembled to fully exploded, plus buttons for Assembled, Exploded, Movement (turns the watch over to look through the sapphire caseback) and Cinematic (autoplays the film);
- the hands show the real current local time and the movement runs live;
- a working chronograph: clicking the 2 o'clock pusher starts and stops it, clicking the 4 o'clock pusher resets it, and the mechanism visibly responds (the column wheel indexes, the clutch engages, the hammers drop onto the heart cams and the hands fly back to zero);
- hovering or clicking any part highlights it and shows its name (e.g. "Escape wheel, 15 teeth");
- smooth: 50+ fps at 1080p on an RTX-class GPU (use instancing or merged geometry where it helps).
- It also has a deterministic render mode for video capture, e.g. `chronograph.html?render=1` exposing `window.renderFrame(timeSeconds)` that poses everything for that time and renders exactly one frame, with no dependence on wall-clock time (re-rendering a frame gives the identical image).
2. `chronograph.mp4`: the cinematic film, rendered from that same HTML file.
- 1080x1080 (square), 60 fps, exactly 30.0 seconds (1800 frames), H.264 High profile, yuv420p, CRF 18 or lower, `-movflags +faststart`, no audio.
- No on-screen text, captions, watermarks or UI in the video. The watch is the whole show.
- The storyboard is in "The film" below.
3. `stills/`: 6-8 PNG frames from the film at 1080x1080 (assembled hero, dial macro, the full exploded view, a movement macro, the balance and escapement close-up, the reassembled final shot).
4. `NOTES.md`: short: what you built, key techniques, the number of distinct parts and total meshes, the exact render command, and your start time, finish time and total build time.

## The watch (model it to scale: 1 unit = 1 mm)
A 42 mm luxury automatic column-wheel chronograph in the tradition of haute horlogerie. Invent a fictional maker's name for the dial and caseback; no real brand names or logos.

Case and exterior:
- Case 42 mm across, about 14 mm thick, about 50 mm lug to lug, 20 mm between the lugs. Built from lathe and loft profiles with real chamfers: mirror-polished bevels alternating with finely brushed flats, and every edge carrying a small bevel that catches a highlight. Polished bezel with an engraved tachymeter scale, a screw-down crown with a knurled grip and an engraved emblem, two chronograph pushers, spring bars, gaskets.
- Domed sapphire crystal with real transmission and refraction (IOR about 1.77), real thickness, distortion at the edge, a faint blue-violet anti-reflective sheen, and reflections of the studio.
- A sapphire exhibition caseback held by screws, with an engraved text ring.
- An alligator leather strap: procedural scale pattern with grain, contrast stitching, padded edges, and a polished pin buckle.

Dial (layered, with real depth):
- Sunray-brushed or guilloché main dial whose anisotropic reflection turns as the light moves; applied, faceted, polished hour markers with lume plots; a printed minute track and tachymeter; three recessed sub-dials with a concentric snailed finish (30-minute counter, 12-hour counter, running seconds); a date window showing a real date disc under the dial; the printed maker's name.
- Hands: faceted dauphine or leaf hour and minute hands with lume inlay, a slim central chronograph seconds hand with a counterweight, sub-dial hands, polished hand caps. The hands sit at realistic heights above the dial and cast soft shadows onto it.

Movement (the star of the exploded view; every part a real, separately modelled 3D object):
- About 30 mm across: a main plate with perlage, bridges with Côtes de Genève stripes and polished anglage (chamfered edges), gold-filled engravings.
- Mainspring barrel with a toothed rim, ratchet wheel and click; the going train (centre, third, fourth and escape wheels) with actually cut teeth, crossed-out spokes, pinions and arbors; a 15-tooth club-tooth escape wheel; a pallet fork with two ruby pallet stones; a balance wheel with timing screws, and a hairspring that is a real Archimedean spiral of at least 12 coils that breathes as the balance swings.
- Chronograph works: a castellated column wheel, the coupling clutch, the chronograph runner, the minute counter wheel, heart cams and reset hammers, and the operating levers.
- Keyless works (winding stem, crown wheel, ratchet wheel, setting lever, yoke), motion works under the dial (cannon pinion, minute wheel, hour wheel), and the date disc with its jumper.
- A skeletonised gold automatic rotor with engraving and a ball-bearing centre.
- 30+ ruby jewels in gold chatons (deep red, translucent) and heat-blued steel screws with slotted heads (thin-film iridescent blue).
- At least 150 distinct parts in total (every screw counts), each a separately named object.

## Mechanical truth (this will be judged closely)
- Tooth counts and gear ratios are self-consistent: the fourth wheel (running seconds) turns once per 60 s, the centre wheel once per hour, the hour wheel once per 12 h. The balance beats at 4 Hz (28,800 vph), so the seconds hands advance in 1/8 s steps. Meshing pairs turn in opposite directions at speeds set by their tooth ratios, phase-aligned so the teeth visibly interlock without passing through each other.
- The escapement visibly works: the balance swings about 270°, the pallet fork flicks between its banking positions, and the escape wheel advances one step per beat.
- The movement keeps running in the exploded view. Parts separate mostly along the watch's axis and stay aligned, like an exploded engineering drawing, so the train still reads as connected.
- Screws unscrew (anticlockwise) as they lift off and screw back in (clockwise) on reassembly.

## Realism (this is where the "wow" comes from)
- PBR throughout with MeshPhysicalMaterial: polished and brushed steel (use anisotropy for the brushing and the sunray dial), rhodium-plated bridges, gold, heat-blued screws (iridescence), rubies and sapphire (transmission, IOR, attenuation colour), a lacquered dial (clearcoat), lume, leather. Procedural normal and roughness maps for every finish, at a resolution that survives macro shots.
- Lighting: a dark, moody luxury studio. A procedural environment (PMREM from a custom scene of large softboxes, strip lights and a dark backdrop; the long strip reflections gliding over polished bevels and the sapphire are what make watches look real), a key light with soft shadows, rim lights to separate the silhouette, contact shadows and ambient occlusion, and a surface for the watch to rest on (dark stone, slate or leather).
- Post-processing: physically based tone mapping (AgX/ACES/Neutral), bloom only on true specular glints, GTAO/SSAO, high-quality anti-aliasing (no jaggies and no shimmering on fine teeth and stripes), macro depth of field with real bokeh and focus pulls, subtle chromatic aberration towards the edges, a vignette and fine grain. Grade it like a flagship watch commercial.
- Render the video frames supersampled (e.g. 2x internal resolution) and downscale for crisp edges.

## The film (30 s)
- 0-6 s: Darkness. A strip light sweeps across the polished case and reveals the watch at a low three-quarter hero angle, hands at 10:10, the running-seconds sub-dial ticking. A macro push-in with a rack focus from the edge of the crystal onto the applied markers.
- 6-9 s: A low, grazing macro past the bezel, crown and pushers. The 2 o'clock pusher clicks and the central chronograph hand starts to sweep.
- 9-16 s: The explosion. The crystal lifts, the bezel rises, the hands and dial float up, then the movement opens layer by layer (bridges, wheels, jewels, screws spinning out) while the strap and caseback drift away the other way. The camera pulls back to reveal the whole exploded constellation, slowly rotating, everything still running.
- 16-23 s: A fly-through down the floating layers: past the swinging balance and breathing hairspring, the ticking pallet fork, the turning train, rubies glowing in the backlight, ending on the rotor's engraving.
- 23-30 s: Reassembly in reverse with precise easing, screws spinning home, a final settle. End on the hero angle at 10:10 with a last glint across the crystal.
- Slow, confident macro camera work, smooth easing, no jerks, no camera clipping through parts unless it is a deliberate pass between floating layers.

## Rendering the MP4
- Find what this machine has (OS, GPU, Node, Python, ffmpeg/ffprobe, an installed Chromium browser such as Chrome or Edge). If Playwright/Puppeteer aren't installed, install `playwright-core` or `puppeteer-core` locally in your folder and drive the installed browser.
- Make sure WebGL runs on the real GPU (check that `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` reports NVIDIA, not SwiftShader), e.g. with flags `--use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist`, or run headed.
- Capture deterministically, frame by frame, through your render mode and pipe the frames into ffmpeg. Do not screen-record in real time.
- Verify with ffprobe: 1080x1080, 60 fps, 1800 frames, 30.00 s.

## Quality bar: check your own work
Look at your renders (open the PNGs with your image-reading tool) again and again while you build, and critique them harshly, as a master watchmaker and a VFX supervisor would: would a watch collector believe this is a photograph? Are the proportions and thicknesses right? Any faceting on curved surfaces, teeth that don't mesh or that pass through each other, z-fighting, holes, black artifacts, aliasing, flat or plastic-looking metal, blown-out highlights, or empty, under-detailed areas of the movement? Fix it and re-render. Before calling it done, extract and review frames from the finished MP4 (start, every ~3 s, end) at full size. Take the time you need; quality is the only thing that counts.

## Final reply
When done, reply with the absolute paths to `chronograph.html` and `chronograph.mp4`, the ffprobe stats (resolution, fps, frame count, duration, file size), the number of distinct parts, your total build time, and a 3-5 line summary of the film.

summary_zh: 使用 Gemini 4 Neon 制作了一款可在浏览器游玩的塔防游戏，并通过 fal 调用 GPT Image 2.6 生成概念图用于 Blender 建模，同时使用了 Tripo3D 资产和 ElevenLabs 音效。

summary_en: Built a 4K animation of the "And I... am... Iron Man" scene rendered with 107,520 pure 7-bit ASCII characters per frame using Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh), with no Unicode blocks or video overlay.
summary_zh: 使用 Gemini 4 Neon（xhigh）制作了《钢铁侠》经典台词场景的 4K 纯 7 位 ASCII 字符动画，每帧包含 107,520 个字符，未使用 Unicode 方块字符或视频叠加。

summary_en: Built a Three.js scene using Gemini 4 Neon swarm in Antigravity over 4 hours of continuous iteration in a review-compare-return loop.
summary_zh: 创作者使用 Antigravity 中的 Gemini 4 Neon swarm 和 Three.js，通过 4 小时的评审-比较-返回循环迭代构建了一个场景。

summary_en: Created a low-poly 3D animation of Chokmah from Blue Archive using Gemini 4 Neon, a GitHub repository, reference images, and a reference video.
summary_zh: 创作者使用开源仓库、参考图片和参考视频，通过 Gemini 4 Neon 制作了《蔚蓝档案》角色霍克玛的低多边形 3D 动画并进行了细节修改。

prompt.text: build me an impressive physics demo rendered at 60 fps, works well in any browser, and involves clicking your mouse or tapping the screen. maybe something with fluid dynamics?

summary_en: Built a 60 fps WebGL Navier-Stokes fluid dynamics playground with Gemini 4 Neon in Google AI Studio from one prompt, with manual button design tweaks.
summary_zh: 创作者在 Google AI Studio 中用 Gemini 4 Neon 通过一条提示词构建了 60 帧的 WebGL 流体动力学交互网页，并手动微调了按钮设计。

prompt.text: 満ち潮の夜、雨の厳島神社の大鳥居を、写真と見まがうほど写実的に。

summary_en: Compared Gemini 4 Neon (Antigravity) and GPT-6.2 Astra (Codex) building Itsukushima Torii in Blender 5.2 Cycles from the same one-line prompt; asks viewers which looks more photorealistic.
summary_zh: 对比了 Gemini 4 Neon（Antigravity）和 GPT-6.2 Astra（Codex）用同一句提示词在 Blender 5.2 Cycles 中制作严岛大鸟居的效果，未定胜负，由观众评判哪个更逼真。
note: 终审 apimart/claude-opus-5-5: The creator ran their own same-prompt comparison: Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2 Astra each drove Blender to build and render a torii scene.

summary_en: Compared Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Argon on the same prompt of an emerald panther emerging from raw emeralds in a palace, without revealing which model produced which result.
summary_zh: 对比了 Claude Fable 5.2 和 Gemini 4 Argon 使用同一提示词生成宫殿中翡翠堆里跃出的大型猫科动物的效果，作者未揭晓各自对应哪款模型，由观众自行判断。
note: 终审 apimart/claude-opus-5-5: The creator's own same-prompt comparison of Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Fable 5.2; the quoted line paraphrases the prompt rather than giving it.

summary_en: Asked Gemini 4 Neon in Netlify to create NeonMiniDex, a web app where the model selected elemental types and generated a sprite for each, inspired by fofrAI.
summary_zh: 受 fofrAI 启发，在 Netlify 中让 Gemini 4 Neon 制作了 NeonMiniDex 网页应用，由模型自行挑选元素属性并为每种属性生成了对应精灵图。
note: 终审 apimart/claude-opus-5-5: The creator's own web app built by Gemini 4 Neon in Netlify; the prompt is a bare name that means nothing without unseen context.
